**Finding: Deviation (high severity) — Section 15 "Assignment or Transfer" (p0080)**

**What the document says.** Section 15 is the Agreement's only assignment provision: neither party may assign without the other's prior written approval, subject to a single exception for assignment "to a financially responsible affiliate."

**Why it fails the fallback.**
- **No successor/M&A carve-out.** A merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of Client's assets would require TrueLink's consent. Our playbook treats a Customer assignment restriction lacking an M&A carve-out as walk-away territory, and the fallback expressly requires a right to assign to successors.
- **Unqualified consent standard.** Consent is not conditioned on reasonableness, so TrueLink could refuse arbitrarily — including by disputing whether an affiliate is "financially responsible."
- **No competitor bar** on TrueLink's side of the assignment right.

**What is already acceptable.** There is no change-of-control trigger anywhere in the Agreement — searches for "change of control" and "merger" returned nothing, and the term and termination provisions (Sections 13–14) contain no such right. So TrueLink has no exit or re-pricing right on our change of control; only the carve-outs and consent standard need repair.

**Redline proposed (validated, ok:true), at the preferred position.** Client may assign freely to an affiliate or to a successor by merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all assets or equity; TrueLink may assign only with our consent, not unreasonably withheld, and never to a Client competitor; other Client assignments require TrueLink consent not unreasonably withheld; and a Client change of control is confirmed not to be an assignment or a termination/re-pricing trigger.

The comment offers the mutual successor-on-written-notice fallback as a landing zone if TrueLink resists the asymmetry.
